public_rationale: Contemporary evaluations document recurring commonsense failures across several domains. Other tasks produced strong results, which matters: the evidence supports uneven reliability, not general inability to answer commonsense questions. That narrower conclusion matches the ordinary reading of struggling repeatedly.
limitations: The evidence covers tested models and benchmarks, not every LLM or everyday situation.
Exact experiment dates are not consistently reported; event dates retain the evaluation year.
Benchmark errors can include ambiguity or cautious refusals as well as reasoning failures.

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is recurring commonsense errors across tasks, despite substantial successful performance. It does not assert universal failure or absence of all commonsense knowledge.
Use 2023 through publication as the contemporary evaluation period. These models have no regular reporting quarter, and the claim names no narrower period.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporary systematic evaluations document repeated errors across multiple commonsense domains or question sets.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative contemporary evaluations establish consistently reliable commonsense reasoning across varied tasks, with the alleged recurring failures explained by invalid questions or scoring errors.

evidence.explanation: The study reports ChatGPT accuracy below 70% on social, event, and temporal commonsense datasets. It also acknowledges strong performance elsewhere, supporting recurring weaknesses rather than blanket incapacity.

ChatGPT answered 27 of 30 CommonsenseQA items, 25 of 30 PiQA items, and 28 of 30 Pep-3k items correctly. This limits any sweeping interpretation of struggle, but remains compatible with repeated errors across other domains.
